props.gloss_en: one who slaughters for the sake of mountains, hills, seas, rivers or wildernesses -- his slaughter is invalid
two holding a knife and slaughtering, one for the sake of one of these and one for the sake of a legitimate thing -- the slaughter is invalid
the mishna says 'invalid' -- yes; offerings to the dead -- no
the baraita: one who slaughters for mountains, hills, rivers, wildernesses, sun and moon, stars and constellations, Michael the great prince, or a small worm -- these are offerings to the dead
Abaye: this [the mishna] is where he said 'to the mountain'
Abaye: that [the baraita] is where he said 'to the gad (angel) of the mountain'
Rav Huna: another's animal was crouching before an idol -- once one cut one siman in it, he forbade it
although they said: one who bows to another's animal has not forbidden it
if he performed an act upon it, he forbade it
the baraita: one who slaughters a sin offering on Shabbat outside [the Temple] for idol worship is liable three sin offerings
Rav Pappa: here we deal with a bird sin offering, where all [three liabilities] come together
Rav Huna stated his ruling per Ulla, and Ulla said: any act at all [forbids]
rather: where he says he worships it at the completion of the slaughter
Mar Zutra in Rav Pappa's name: where half the windpipe was deficient and he added any amount to it and completed it -- all come together
Rav Pappa: were it not that Rav Huna said 'one siman', the chatat would be no refutation of him -- [one could say] what is 'an act'? a significant act
Rav Pappa: were it not that Rav Huna said 'another's animal', the chatat would be no refutation of him -- for his own he can forbid, another's he cannot
lest you say that since he acquires it for atonement it is like his own -- he teaches us [it is not]
a person does not render forbidden a thing that is not his
since he acquires it for atonement, it is like his own
here [the mishna of two holding a knife] he has a partnership share in it
the mishna: one who renders [another's food] impure, mixes teruma [into it], or pours [his wine] as a libation -- unwittingly exempt, deliberately liable
here too he has a partnership share in it
a gentile who poured a Jew's wine as a libation not in the presence of an idol -- he forbade it
R' Yehuda ben Beteira and R' Yehuda ben Bava permit it
first reason: wine is poured as a libation only in the presence of an idol
second reason: he can say to him, it is not within your power to forbid my wine against my will
the stam: [the dispute whether a person forbids what is not his] is like [the dispute of] the tannaim of the libation baraita
even per the one who says a person forbids what is not his -- that applies to a gentile
but a Jew intends [only] to distress him
here [the mishna of two holding a knife] we deal with a Jewish apostate
here too [the Gittin mishna] a Jewish apostate
one who was warned and accepted the warning permitted himself to death -- there is no greater apostate than he
